note: Which reading of a homograph the word before it makes likely. A spelling that is several words is decided by what surrounds it, and the cheapest signal that works in every language is the part of speech of the neighbour: a determiner is followed by a noun, an infinitive marker by a verb. The parts of speech are the dump's own, and a neighbour whose own reading is ambiguous says nothing rather than guessing. 'after' is the part of speech of the word before; 'prefers' is what the homograph is then read as; 'margin' is how much more the preferred reading has to be worth than the runner-up before the card stops offering the choice, counted in these votes.

rules.why: a determiner introduces a noun phrase
the same, where the dump calls it that
an adjective modifies the noun after it
a pronoun subject takes a verb
an infinitive marker: to book, zu buchen
an auxiliary takes a participle or infinitive
an adverb before a word modifies a verb
a preposition governs a noun phrase
a clause after a conjunction begins again
